item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Tuesday, 11 August 2026
item.description:
Stargrace hits level 46, braves the planes, blows 150 motes on an accidental bard charm upgrade, then swaps classes again.

Ocho gushes about Woodland Warriors, where a slime-slinging bullfrog and friends show off how flexible, beginner-friendly Many Worlds can be.

Nimgimli finds The Planet Crafter bleak but intriguing, with early survival shaped by tight oxygen limits, light death penalties, and lots of little fallback bases.

Shintar ranks SWTOR: Legacy of the Sith’s standout NPCs, praising how character-driven the expansion became, especially Rass Ordo and Darth Nul.

Krista highlights Cozy Marbles as a chill marble-run builder packed with creative pieces, playful customization, and easygoing race setup.

Wilhelm logs into No Man’s Sky’s 10th anniversary meetup, dances in the Anomaly, and enjoys the game’s fleeting, friendly stranger encounters.

Anarchae rounds up Blaugust links, indie web tools, Echofeed’s shutdown, and a handy reminder to back up Letterboxd just in case.

Jamie Zawinski marks Hackers’ 31st anniversary with a Cyberdelia night of movie screening, costume contest, Wipeout XL, skate ramps, and dancing.

Juhis gives a brisk Python intro to JSON validation with Pydantic, using Pokédex data to show how schemas catch bad input.

Ramen Junkie looks back on building a Raspberry Pi-powered PiGrrl 2 handheld that worked, barely, and got outclassed by newer emulation devices.

Dave Winer checks in on RSS.chat, cable-streaming sprawl, and recommends The Agency if polished British-style crime stories are your thing.

Tipa explains how Discord fatigue led her to build the AI-powered Daily Blogroll from Python, RSS, and TerraChat tech repurposed from Final Fantasy VI fandom.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Monday, 10 August 2026
item.description:
Tipa digs into EverQuest Legends nostalgia, chasing classic class armor and old quest memories even when newer gear makes the whole thing gloriously unnecessary.

Nicole tours 1991’s Idol Mahjong Final Romance, a stylish strip-riichi oddity with fixed dates, item-shop quirks, and more aesthetic than later entries.

Wilhelm checks Fantasy Critic Week 32, where Big Walk surged, Beast of Reincarnation landed softer, and the standings got a nice late shake-up.

Wolfy is still steamed at CIG, but also finds brighter gaming notes in Aion 2’s clearer pitch, Skate’s big multiplayer test, and Dead As Disco’s auto-BPM tool.

Andrew Plotkin rounds up new Anglerfish details: Cyan’s Myst-universe pitch impressed publishers, missed funding, triggered layoffs, and left smaller follow-up Mudfish intriguing.

CrazyKinux hypes Dark Matter season two, praising season one’s Box-and-alternate-realities mind-bender and making a solid case for a pre-premiere binge.

Joel shares a brisk personal fact file covering origami, handheld gaming, speedcubing, favorite colors, and a few cheerfully contrarian food opinions.

Warner’s weekly reading roundup roams from human origins and AI religion to writing accuracy, political moderation, and the data-center backlash.

Tim Bray posts some handsome West African drums and explains how a weekly jam pushed him from curious stand-in to buying his own dunun setup.

Tan mixes a warm personal update with a Blaugust link roundup touching Morrowind, Final Fantasy VII, FUTO keyboard, indie platforms, and EdTech.

Wakupan shares hobby talk spanning doujin fandom, marathon solo karaoke, tarot study, and a heartfelt love of reading, theater, and fiction itself.

Roger takes the Blaugust superpower prompt and sensibly swerves past Superman-style heroics and time travel, both sounding like more trouble than they’re worth.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Sunday, 9 August 2026
item.description:
Tipa marks turning 65 by tallying a startling lifetime in EverQuest, EQ2, and a long parade of MMORPGs.

Frostilyte digs into a low-tier Pokémon Silver run, where Johto’s time-based catches and weekday events make early planning surprisingly fiddly.

Magi highlights Yashi – Sand Driver, a cozy desert survival road trip about van upgrades, scavenging, and chasing New Eden with your coyote.

Shintar looks back on WoW: Midnight Season 1, praising better-tuned delves while warning Blizzard’s steady reward drip could tip into burnout.

Ellie finally finishes Trails in the Sky and finds a decent JRPG that doesn’t quite match the towering hype around the series.

The Friendly Necromancer survives EverQuest Legends server drama, finishes up Najena, dings 30, and heads into the Guks with new AA toys.

Bhagpuss starts a drawer-diving series with old Legion of Superheroes stickers and the strange half-memory of forgotten collectibles.

Cristian’s quick reminder: even on Linux, occasional scans with ClamAV, rkhunter, chkrootkit, and Lynis are just sensible housekeeping.

Aneesh is fed up with online ‘hard disagree’ energy that shuts down curiosity instead of adding anything thoughtful or playful.

UltrViolet wrestles with Blaugust motivation, draft-post anxiety, and the curious pull of trying EverQuest Legends for its solo play.

Kluwes reflects on ten years of Many Welps, from almost becoming a book blogger to finding a lasting home in games writing.

Wilhelm riffs on Aftermath’s Hater Week, Adobe misery, overplayed charts, and why bloggers probably shouldn’t pretend to be above strong opinions.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Saturday, 8 August 2026
item.description:
Aywren breaks down FFXIV patch 7.55’s Phantom Relic grind, from crafted items to roulettes, Occult Crescent drops, and the inevitable tome sink.

John loves how It Consumes turns darkness and limited light into a tense roguelite shooter loop full of unlocks, timing, and doomed runs.

Tipa digs through EverQuest Legends’ cash shop, where ornamentation and convenience items look pricey even if the store isn’t pay-to-win yet.

Joar says FFXIV is excellent, but its huge story focus, alt-job leveling style, and WoW muscle memory kept it from becoming home.

Owls celebrates finally hitting level 50 in EverQuest Legends, then immediately sets sights on killing Innoruuk and retracing an old necromancer route.

Welsh Troll reads ESO’s revised roadmap as delays, QoL triage, and a worrying hint that broader Elder Scrolls collaboration could sideline the MMO.

Marc pushes back on Donkey Kong 3 revisionism, arguing Nintendo’s arcade exit was really about shifting focus to Famicom and NES.

Wilhelm tears into Xbox Games’ layoffs, fuzzy “Four Cs,” Minecraft fixation, and pricier consoles, arguing Microsoft still looks directionless.

Jimmy traces how Will Wright’s Oakland firestorm experience fed into the life-sim thinking that would eventually shape The Sims.

Jeff comes away impressed by Dell’s XPS 13 and Intel’s Core 5 320, especially Fedora 44 support and standout x86 efficiency.

Axxuy reflects on drafting by hand versus Neovim, arguing blogs lose none of the words but gain something irreplaceably webby through links.

Azuriel argues AI-generated blog images and bot-like replies trade away the human messiness that makes blogging and online communities worth showing up for.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Friday, 7 August 2026
item.description:
Tipa dives into Pokopia’s flooded Cerulean City expansion, rebuilding ruins, collecting a separate 50-mon dex, and testing underwater life with Ditto’s new Dive command.

Sey rounds up Wholesome Games Celebration picks, spotlighting fresh demos like Wild n Chill, A Tiny Wander, Tony the Mole, and Jigrift.

Mailvaltar stuck with Wuthering Waves after the Edgerunners collab and ended up loving its flashy combat and enemy-drop Echo grind more than expected.

Wilhelm’s Stardew Valley farm hits summer goals, repairs the bus, nabs a sandfish in Calico Desert, and gets a rude reminder combat has teeth.

Ghastly digs into 3DS upgrade FOMO, pushing back on inflated resale hype and asking whether another handheld is actually worth it.

Tobold finds Pathfinder: Wrath of the Righteous’ Treasure of the Midnight Isles a neat build-testing roguelike, but too thin on story to stick.

Michael’s take is blunt: game devs should stop using LLMs altogether, citing theft, community pollution, and huge energy costs.

Blockade85 vents about real life slowing progress in Warframe and Final Fantasy VII, while admitting the small gains feel sweeter now.

Joar writes candidly about the ‘empty nest’ not arriving as one clean moment, but as a quieter, messier shift even with a son nearby.

Bruce Schneier flags that ICE is reportedly buying credit-card application data through brokers, which is as unsettling as it sounds.

Brennan reflects on EchoFeed shutting down, blogging’s fragility, and why writing online still matters as a way to leave something behind.

Kimimi finally ships Terror of the Alien Mindmasters, reworking a stalled C64 idea into a browser-playable Twine sci-fi interactive fiction.
